\[
\boxed{(P_{m,k},N_{m,k})=\left((m+2)2^{m-1},\;m2^{m-1}\right)}
\]

Let
\[
e_m(z)=\exp\left(\frac{2\pi i z}{2^m}\right).
\]
For
\[
G_m(a)=\sum_{u\bmod 2^m} e_m(au^2),
\]
with \(a\) odd, we use the standard 2-adic Gauss evaluation, derived by separating even and odd terms:
\[
G_m(a)=
\begin{cases}
2^{m/2}(1+i^a),&m\text{ even},\\
2^{(m+1)/2}e^{2\pi i a/8},&m\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Also,
\[
\sum_{x\bmod 2^m}e_m(x^2+bx)=0
\]
if \(b\) is odd, while if \(b=2c\), completing the square gives
\[
\sum_{x\bmod 2^m}e_m(x^2+2cx)=e_m(-c^2)G_m(1).
\]

Apply this to the \(x\)-sum with \(b=y-r\). Only \(y\equiv r\pmod 2\) contributes. Write \(y=r+2t\), \(t\bmod 2^{m-1}\). Then
\[
A_{m,k}(r,s)
=G_m(1)e_m(2^kr^2-sr)
\sum_{t\bmod 2^{m-1}}
e_m\left((2^{k+2}-1)t^2+2(2^kr-s)t\right).
\]
Let
\[
a=2^{k+2}-1,\qquad C=2^kr-s.
\]
Since \(a\) is odd, the last sum is half of the complete sum modulo \(2^m\):
\[
\sum_{t\bmod 2^{m-1}} e_m(at^2+2Ct)
=\frac12 e_m(-a^{-1}C^2)G_m(a).
\]
Thus
\[
A_{m,k}(r,s)
=\frac12G_m(1)G_m(a)\,
e_m\left(2^kr^2-sr-a^{-1}(2^kr-s)^2\right).
\]

Now \(a=2^{k+2}-1\equiv -1\pmod 8\). Therefore \(G_m(1)G_m(a)\) is a positive real number for both parities of \(m\): for even \(m\), the phases are \(\zeta_8\) and \(\zeta_8^{-1}\); for odd \(m\), likewise. Hence the sign/realness of \(A_{m,k}(r,s)\) is determined only by the final root of unity.

Put \(C=2^kr-s\). Since \((r,s)\mapsto(r,C)\) is a bijection modulo \(2^m\), and
\[
2^kr^2-sr-a^{-1}C^2
=Cr-a^{-1}C^2
=C(r-a^{-1}C),
\]
the exponent runs exactly over products \(Ct\) with \(C,t\bmod 2^m\).

So \(A_{m,k}(r,s)\) is positive real iff
\[
Ct\equiv 0\pmod {2^m},
\]
and negative real iff
\[
Ct\equiv 2^{m-1}\pmod {2^m}.
\]

Count residues modulo \(2^m\) by 2-adic valuation. There are \(2^{m-j-1}\) residues with valuation \(j<m\), and one residue, \(0\), with valuation \(m\).

For positivity, fix \(v_2(C)=j<m\). Then \(t\) must be divisible by \(2^{m-j}\), giving \(2^j\) choices, hence
\[
2^{m-j-1}\cdot 2^j=2^{m-1}
\]
pairs for each \(j=0,\dots,m-1\). If \(C=0\), there are \(2^m\) choices for \(t\). Therefore
\[
P_{m,k}=m2^{m-1}+2^m=(m+2)2^{m-1}.
\]

For negativity, we need
\[
v_2(C)+v_2(t)=m-1.
\]
For each \(j=0,\dots,m-1\), this gives
\[
2^{m-j-1}\cdot 2^j=2^{m-1}
\]
pairs, so
\[
N_{m,k}=m2^{m-1}.
\]

Thus, for every allowed \(m,k\),
\[
\boxed{(P_{m,k},N_{m,k})=\left((m+2)2^{m-1},\;m2^{m-1}\right)}.
\]
